sections.heading: C — Traffic laws, traffic light signals and road signs
sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic laws, traffic light signals and road signs

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A108
Traffic laws can change, the current rules of the road can be found by searching RCW 46.61 online, and staying informed is your job for as long as you drive. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A108
Drive on the right side of the road, using the left side only briefly to pass safely and legally on a two-lane road. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A108
On roads with several lanes going your way, keep right except to pass, use the left lane for passing slower traffic, and obey the speed limit even while passing. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A108
Carpool lanes are not passing lanes, and you should not pass or drive on the shoulder unless officials or signs tell you to. [A108]
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A108
Never drive in reverse on the road even if you miss a turn or exit, because backing up on a shoulder or freeway is illegal. [A108]
Why it matters: a missed turn or exit never justifies reversing on the road.
Source: [A108 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A109
Hitchhiking and picking up hitchhikers on Washington freeways are both illegal. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A109
Traffic control devices are the signals, signs and road markings that direct traffic, and you are responsible for spotting and obeying all of them. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A109
Police, construction and maintenance workers and school crossing guards may direct traffic in special situations, and their directions override the signals and must be obeyed. [A109]
Why it matters: a person directing traffic outranks the light.
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A109
At a traffic signal that is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop: stop completely, yield to traffic on your right, and go carefully when safe. [A109]
Source: [A109 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0109]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A110
At a solid red light, stop and wait for green and a clear intersection, though after a full stop you may turn right if no sign forbids a turn on red and there is room to enter traffic. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A110
After a complete stop at a red light, you may also turn left onto a one-way street when no sign prohibits it and there is room to merge. [A110]
Why it matters: for this left turn on red, the street you turn onto must be one-way.
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A110
A flashing red light works exactly like a stop sign, while a red arrow means you may not go in the arrow's direction. [A110]
Source: [A110 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0110]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A111
A solid yellow light warns that red is coming, so slow and prepare to stop, but if you are already in the intersection keep going at the posted speed, never speeding up to beat it. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A111
A flashing yellow light means the same as a yield sign, so treat the intersection as uncontrolled and go only when you have the right-of-way. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A111
A yellow arrow warns that the arrow will soon turn red, so get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic. [A111]
Source: [A111 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0111]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A112
A solid green light means go once the intersection is clear, still yielding to pedestrians and to emergency vehicles as the law requires. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A112
Turning left on a solid green, oncoming traffic has the right-of-way, so wait where you can see approaching cars and turn when there is a gap. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A112
Washington does not use flashing green lights, though British Columbia uses them to warn that pedestrians are waiting to cross. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A112
A green arrow gives you the right-of-way in its direction, with no oncoming, crossing or pedestrian traffic expected while it shows. [A112]
Source: [A112 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0112]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A113
A freeway ramp meter works like a normal signal: on red stop at the white stop line, and on green continue up the ramp. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A113
Sign colors carry meaning: red for prohibited or restricted actions, orange for construction warnings, yellow for general warnings, white for regulations, green for guidance, blue for motorist services and brown for recreation and culture. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A113
Fluorescent yellow-green signs warn of school, pedestrian and bicycle activity. [A113]
Source: [A113 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0113]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A114
At a stop sign, stop at the line, crosswalk or corner, check all directions for vehicles and pedestrians, and yield the right-of-way, while a yield sign means slow down and let traffic with the right-of-way go first. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A114
A posted maximum speed applies to ideal conditions, so you can be ticketed for going too fast for slippery or foggy conditions even below the limit. [A114]
Why it matters: driving under the posted limit is not automatically legal.
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A114
Some roads post a minimum speed limit, and you must drive at least that fast so you do not endanger other drivers. [A114]
Source: [A114 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0114]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A115
Automated traffic safety cameras record drivers who fail to stop for a steady red light or a railroad crossing signal or who speed in a school zone, their locations are clearly marked, and tickets are mailed to the vehicle owner. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A115
Speed warning signs recommend a slower speed for a hazard such as a curve, and digital variable speed limit signs change posted limits and can close lanes ahead of slow traffic. [A115]
Source: [A115 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A116
A red circle with a red slash over a symbol forbids that action, such as a left turn, right turn or U-turn. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A116
A Do Not Enter sign is square with a white horizontal bar inside a circle, and a Wrong Way sign means you are headed against traffic and must stop and turn around at once. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A116
A shared center left-turn lane is reserved for drivers turning left from either direction and may not be used for through travel or passing. [A116]
Source: [A116 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A117
In a highway work zone everyone must yield to workers, equipment and vehicles with flashing yellow lights, and fines double for offenses there when workers are present. [A117]
Why it matters: the doubling depends on workers being present.
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A117
Service signs point to services such as hospitals, electric vehicle charging stations and rest areas. [A117]
Source: [A117 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A118
Destination signs give directions and distances to places such as cities and airports, and the shape and color of a route number sign tell you whether it is an interstate, U.S., state, city or county road. [A118]
Source: [A118 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A119
The guide shows only some Washington signs, yet drivers are responsible for knowing every sign, including city and county ones. [A119]
Source: [A119 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A120
An added lane sign marks a lane that joins from the right where no merging is required. [A120]
Source: [A120 -> src:rdmv-wa-s:washington-state-department-of-licensing:handbook:pdf-0120]

Glossary: traffic control device — a signal, sign or road marking that directs traffic [A109]. Ramp meter — a signal on a freeway on-ramp [A113]. Regulatory sign — a white sign stating a rule [A113]. Flashing yellow — a signal with the same meaning as a yield sign [A111]. Work zone — a construction or maintenance area on the highway [A117].
Memory aid: flashing red acts like a stop sign and flashing yellow acts like a yield sign [A110] [A111].

items.skill: recognizing traffic signs by shape, color and symbol
items.why: sign recognition is visual and needs sign images, which the extracted page text does not carry

items.skill: choosing the right action for each signal state
items.why: solid, flashing and arrow signals in three colors form a matrix that is best drilled signal by signal

corpus_stability.reason: The Washington Driver Guide is one published guide revision (form line 520-400 R/4/25 on physical p4); the guide itself notes it may lag recent legislative changes, and nothing on the selected pages indicates more than one rewrite per year.
